(f) It does have composite/blend modes but no SVG filter graph and no built-in Gaussian blur, so it would not close the blur/shadow gap either. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: DOMINATED in this context — resvg ships a working wasm today, Blend2D cannot ship one. Reconsider only if you ever add a native Node render service for batch export, where its JIT throughput genuinely beats everything else in this list.

entries.name: tiny-skia (linebender/tiny-skia)
entries.what_it_is: 'A tiny Skia subset ported to Rust', 1.6k stars, version 0.12.0. THIS IS THE ENGINE ALREADY INSIDE YOUR ADOPTED @resvg/resvg-wasm — resvg rasterises through tiny-skia. Verified from docs.rs that these public types exist: PathBuilder, PathStroker, Stroke, StrokeDash, Mask, Pattern, LinearGradient, RadialGradient, Transform, Pixmap, and BlendMode. I pulled the full BlendMode variant list: Clear, Source, Destination, SourceOver, DestinationOver, SourceIn, DestinationIn, SourceOut, DestinationOut, SourceAtop, DestinationAtop, Xor, Plus, Modulate, Screen, Overlay, Darken, Lighten, ColorDodge, ColorBurn, HardLight, SoftLight, Difference, Exclusion, Multiply, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity — 29 variants, i.e. the complete Porter-Duff + separable + non-separable CSS/SVG set. Adds ~200 KiB to a binary and compiles in under 5 seconds.
entries.license: BSD-3-Clause — the About sidebar says BSD-3-Clause and the README states 'The same as used by Skia: New BSD License'. Note: this CORRECTS the assumption in the brief that it is MIT/Apache dual — it is not, it is BSD-3-Clause (still fully permissive and fine for you).
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No standalone prebuilt .wasm on npm under its own name — BUT you already ship it transitively inside @resvg/resvg-wasm's 2.48 MB index_bg.wasm. To get its path API in the browser you would write a thin Rust crate exposing fill_path/stroke_path/etc. via wasm-bindgen and build with wasm-pack. (c) The Rust-side footprint is stated as ~200 KiB of code; a wasm-bindgen wrapper exposing just the drawing API should land in the few-hundred-kB range — dramatically smaller than the 2.48 MB resvg build, because you drop the entire SVG parser, filter graph and font stack.
entries.language_stack: Rust, no unsafe-heavy deps, SIMD via x86-64 AVX and AArch64 NEON intrinsics; the wasm32 target works but SIMD there is not advertised.
entries.last_activity: 0.12.0; moved into the linebender org, actively maintained alongside resvg/kurbo/vello.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) NO TEXT AT ALL. 'Text rendering (maybe someday)' is listed verbatim under Out of scope; the README says 'The main missing feature is text rendering'. That is not a defect for an Arabic app — it is neutral. You shape with harfrust/harfbuzzjs, convert glyphs to outlines, and hand tiny-skia plain paths. It never assumes pre-shaped Latin runs because it never sees text.
entries.steal_this_idea: PathStroker as a first-class, reusable object rather than a stroke() call. It converts a path + Stroke params into a NEW Path — that is real stroke-to-path OUTLINING, the operation Illustrator calls 'Outline Stroke'. Being able to materialise the outline means you can then boolean it, gradient-fill it, or export it as an SVG <path> instead of a stroked path — which is exactly what your PDF/SVG exporters want for fidelity. Also note the stroker is a persistent object so its scratch buffers are reused across thousands of calls.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) FULL PATH API: PathBuilder with move_to/line_to/quad_to/cubic_to/close, fill and stroke, Transform, Mask for clipping. (e) STROKE-TO-PATH: YES via PathStroker — one of only two things in this sweep that does it (the other being kurbo). Dashing: yes (StrokeDash). Joins/caps/miter: yes via Stroke. Boolean ops: NO — 'Advanced Bézier path operations' is explicitly out of scope; pair with pathkit-wasm. (f) BLEND MODES: YES, all 29 — this alone closes a third of EXELMJ's blur/shadow/blend blank. SVG FILTERS AND BLUR: NO, not in tiny-skia itself; the filter graph lives one level up in resvg. (h) Sync — it is a plain CPU rasteriser writing into a Pixmap, no async anywhere; only the wasm module instantiation is async. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: it IS resvg's engine, so at the shipped-artifact level it is DOMINATED (you already have it). But at the SOURCE level it COMPLEMENTS strongly: exposing tiny-skia directly gets you the interactive path API + 29 blend modes + stroke outlining that resvg's SVG-in/PNG-out wrapper hides from you, in a much smaller binary.

entries.name: @resvg/resvg-wasm (THE INCUMBENT — baseline for all comparisons)
entries.what_it_is: The already-ADOPTED package. Registry JSON verified: version 2.6.2, license MPL-2.0, main index.js, types index.d.ts, dist.unpackedSize 2,526,600 bytes, repo github.com/yisibl/resvg-js. I read index.d.ts in full: exports `initWasm()` (async), class `Resvg(svgData: Uint8Array|string, opts?)` with render() -> RenderedImage, toString(), innerBBox()/getBBox(), cropByBBox(bbox), imagesToResolve()/resolveImage(), width/height; RenderedImage exposes asPng() -> Uint8Array and a raw `pixels` RGBA property. Options: font (system fonts, custom font buffers, family overrides), fitTo (original|width|height|zoom), background (CSS3 colors), crop, dpi, languages, shapeRendering/textRendering/imageRendering.
entries.license: MPL-2.0 — from the npm registry `license` field on 2.6.2. IMPORTANT FINDING: the UPSTREAM resvg project has RELICENSED. github.com/linebender/resvg now shows 'Apache-2.0 and MIT' (dual) in its About sidebar, and usvg 0.48.1 on docs.rs is 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT'. So a newer resvg build would be Apache/MIT, not MPL — strictly better for your constraint. The npm wasm package is pinned to the older MPL-2.0 lineage.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) PREBUILT — this is its great strength. npm i @resvg/resvg-wasm and you are done. (c) index_bg.wasm = 2.48 MB exactly (read from unpkg's listing for 2.6.2); index.js 18 kB, index.mjs 17 kB, index.min.js 8.59 kB, index.d.ts 2.5 kB. (h) Init is ASYNC: `await initWasm(wasmModuleOrURL)` must resolve before any Resvg construction.
entries.language_stack: Rust (resvg + usvg + tiny-skia) compiled via wasm-bindgen; JS/TS wrapper.
entries.last_activity: 2.6.2 on npm; upstream resvg at linebender is very active (usvg 0.48.1 released 2 Aug 2026), so the npm wasm build lags upstream considerably.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) THE ONE ENGINE IN THIS SWEEP THAT ALREADY DOES ARABIC PROPERLY — and it is the one you already have. usvg's own docs list optional dependencies on `harfrust` (shaping) and `unicode-bidi` (bidirectional text), and state that text is 'completely resolved', i.e. converted to paths. The npm 2.6.2 build predates the harfrust switch and uses rustybuzz, which shapes Arabic correctly for any normal OpenType Arabic font (its only documented gap is the FALLBACK shaper for fonts lacking OpenType Arabic features, not the OpenType path itself). Practical upshot: you can hand resvg an SVG containing raw Arabic <text> + a font buffer and get correctly shaped, correctly ordered, outlined Arabic back. NOTHING ELSE HERE DOES THAT OUT OF THE BOX.
entries.steal_this_idea: usvg as a stage, not a renderer. usvg 0.48.1 takes messy real-world SVG and RESOLVES it: <use> expanded, nested <svg> flattened, CSS applied, relative units resolved, external/base64 images inlined, basic shapes converted to paths, markers converted to regular elements, and TEXT CONVERTED TO PATHS with harfrust shaping and unicode-bidi ordering. Run every imported SVG through resvg/usvg first and your hand-written designApp.ts only ever has to understand paths, gradients and images — it never needs a CSS engine, a marker resolver or a text shaper. That is the single highest-leverage architectural idea in this whole sweep and you can adopt it with the package you already have.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Stated as the BASELINE so every other verdict is meaningful. Its weaknesses, concretely: (d) NO PATH API — you cannot moveTo/cubicTo/fill/stroke/clip; it is strictly whole-file SVG-string-in, PNG-or-RGBA-out, which makes it useless for interactive editing (you would re-serialise and re-render the entire document per mouse move). (e) No exposed stroke-to-path, no dash control, no boolean ops at the API surface. (f) It DOES have the full SVG filter graph internally — I enumerated usvg::filter and it contains GaussianBlur, DropShadow, Blend, ColorMatrix, Composite, Flood, Morphology, Turbulence, DisplacementMap, Tile, Image, Offset, Merge, DiffuseLighting, SpecularLighting — so EXELMJ is NOT entirely without blur/shadow today, it just cannot reach them except by writing <filter> markup into an SVG string and re-rendering the whole file. That is the real state of the 'total blank'. (h) Async init, one-shot render — fundamentally the wrong latency shape for a live canvas.

entries.name: resvg / usvg upstream (linebender/resvg)
entries.what_it_is: The upstream Rust source of your incumbent, now under the linebender org. 4.0k stars, 336 forks, 1,217 commits on main. usvg 0.48.1 released 2 Aug 2026. usvg exports Tree, Group, Path, Text, Image, Fill, Stroke, gradients, ClipPath, Mask and a full `filter` module. The README states resvg has 'no external non-Rust dependencies' and is 'guaranteed to work everywhere where you can compile Rust itself, including WASM'; the CLI binary is under 5 MB. It targets the STATIC SVG subset — no <a>, <script>, <view>, <cursor>, no events, no animation.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT (dual) per the About sidebar; usvg 0.48.1 on docs.rs states 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT'. This is a RELICENSE away from the MPL-2.0 that the npm @resvg/resvg-wasm 2.6.2 build carries — materially better for your permissive-only constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Build your own wasm with wasm-pack — that is the entire point of this entry. Doing so lets you (i) pick up the Apache/MIT relicense, (ii) pick up harfrust instead of archived rustybuzz, (iii) feature-gate out what you don't need, and (iv) EXPOSE usvg's Tree to JS so you get a resolved scene graph instead of only a PNG. (c) The existing prebuilt is 2.48 MB; a text-enabled custom build will be similar, a text-disabled one much smaller.
entries.language_stack: Rust; crates usvg (parse/resolve), resvg (raster via tiny-skia), plus the C API and CLI.
entries.last_activity: Very active — usvg 0.48.1 on 2 Aug 2026.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) BEST-IN-CLASS HERE. usvg's optional deps are `harfrust` for shaping and `unicode-bidi` for bidi, and text is 'completely resolved' into paths. For an Arabic-first app this is the only engine in the sweep with both shaping AND bidi already wired, and it emits OUTLINES so downstream rendering needs no text support whatsoever.
entries.steal_this_idea: 'Text is completely resolved' — the decision to make text-to-path a MANDATORY pipeline stage rather than an optional export feature. Every downstream consumer (rasteriser, PDF writer, SVG writer, Illustrator COM bridge, boolean ops) then works on one uniform path representation and none of them needs to know Arabic exists. Given EXELMJ already has hand-written Arabic bidi runs in designApp.ts, adopting this stage-boundary would let you delete Arabic special-casing from every export path you own.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Upgrading from the npm 2.6.2 build to a self-built current resvg is probably the highest value-per-effort move available: better licence (Apache/MIT vs MPL), better shaper (harfrust vs archived rustybuzz), and the option to expose usvg::Tree so EXELMJ can read a RESOLVED scene graph. (f) It carries the complete SVG filter set I enumerated above, so it remains your only credible source of feGaussianBlur/feDropShadow/feBlend/feColorMatrix/feTurbulence semantics. VERDICT vs the npm build: strictly better on licence and text; costs you a Rust/wasm-pack toolchain. It still does NOT give you an interactive path API — for that you go to tiny-skia (its own rasteriser) or ThorVG.

entries.name: vello_cpu (linebender)
entries.what_it_is: 'A CPU-based renderer for Vello, optimized for SIMD and multithreaded execution.' Version 0.2.0, released 7 Aug 2026, ~21K SLoC. Verified public API from docs.rs: RenderContext (the drawing context), Pixmap / PixmapMut (RGBA8 premultiplied), Resources, Mask, CompositeMode and Paint enums; methods fill_path(), stroke_path(), fill_rect(), glyph_run() (behind the default-on `text` feature). Paths are kurbo BezPath, re-exported via vello_common. Two pipelines: u8_pipeline (speed) and f32_pipeline (quality), plus an optional `multithreading` feature.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT — confirmed on lib.rs for 0.2.0 and on docs.rs. Matches the brief exactly.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No prebuilt wasm on npm — Rust crate, you build with wasm-pack/wasm-bindgen. (c) Crate is ~1 MB of source / 21K SLoC; wasm output unmeasured but this is a leaner surface than resvg (no SVG parser, no filter graph, no font DB) so expect well under 2.48 MB. NOTABLE: the crate explicitly documents 'SIMD optimizations for WASM SIMD' — it is one of the very few here that has been deliberately tuned for the wasm32 target rather than merely compiling for it.
entries.language_stack: Rust; no_std capable (needs `std` or `libm`); SIMD for aarch64, x86 AND wasm.
entries.last_activity: 0.2.0 on 7 Aug 2026 — a week old at time of writing. Actively developed.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) glyph_run() consumes GLYPHS, not text — it assumes you have already shaped. That is correct-by-construction for Arabic: pair it with harfrust or harfbuzzjs and it never makes a Latin assumption. It has no built-in layout engine to fight.
entries.steal_this_idea: The sparse strips architecture: instead of rasterising a full-width scanline per path, decompose coverage into sparse horizontal strips so empty space costs nothing and the same data structure can be consumed by a CPU SIMD loop, a WebGL2 fragment shader, or a WebGPU compute shader. For EXELMJ the transferable lesson is the SHARED INTERMEDIATE: encode your scene once into a backend-neutral form, then choose Canvas2D / wasm / GPU at render time without rewriting the scene traversal.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) REAL PATH API — fill_path/stroke_path over kurbo BezPath. (e) Stroking with kurbo's Stroke/Join/Cap/Dashes; boolean ops NOT included (kurbo has no booleans either — pair with pathkit-wasm). (f) BLEND: CompositeMode exists, so composite/blend is covered. FILTERS: explicitly weak — the docs state 'Complex filter graphs are currently not supported at all and will panic. In multi-threaded mode, even simple filters are currently unsupported.' A PANIC in wasm is a hard trap that kills your module instance, so treat filters as unusable here today. (h) SYNC rendering — a plain CPU rasteriser into a Pixmap, which is the closest match in this whole sweep to designApp.ts's synchronous Canvas2D model; only module instantiation is async. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS TODAY, COULD REPLACE IN ~A YEAR. It gives the interactive path API resvg lacks, with a better licence and wasm-SIMD tuning, but resvg still wins decisively on filters (which panic here) and on shaped Arabic text (which vello_cpu doesn't attempt). Track it; do not bet the design module on it at 0.2.0.

entries.name: vello_hybrid (linebender)
entries.what_it_is: 'A hybrid CPU/GPU renderer for 2D vector graphics' — CPU does path processing and geometry setup, GPU does rendering and compositing. Version 0.2.0, released 7 Aug 2026. Two backends: wgpu (default, needs sparse shaders) and, critically, an optional WebGL2 backend using GLSL shaders 'for browser support'.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT — confirmed on lib.rs for 0.2.0.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No prebuilt wasm; Rust + wasm-pack. The `webgl` feature flag is the browser story. (c) Unmeasured. Being GPU-assisted, more of the work lives in shaders and less in the wasm binary than vello_cpu.
entries.language_stack: Rust + wgpu, or Rust + GLSL via WebGL2.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: Same as vello_cpu — glyph-level, no shaping assumptions, safe for Arabic if you shape upstream.
entries.steal_this_idea: THE WEBGL2 FALLBACK DECISION. Vello proper requires WebGPU compute shaders and its own README warns 'The web is not currently a primary target for Vello, and WebGPU implementations are incomplete, so you might run into issues.' vello_hybrid's answer is to move the compute-shaped work back onto the CPU and use only WebGL2 for compositing. For an OFFLINE Electron app that must work on whatever GPU the user's machine has, this 'CPU for geometry, lowest-common-denominator GPU for compositing' split is the correct risk posture — copy the posture even if you don't copy the code.
entries.why_useful_for_us: The realistic GPU-accelerated option for EXELMJ, because unlike Vello proper it does not demand WebGPU. Its own docs admit it is 'slightly less mature than its CPU-only counterpart Vello CPU' and list unsupported mask layers and certain blend modes as known limitations. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS — a different axis entirely (interactive GPU compositing vs one-shot CPU SVG rendering). Not a candidate for adoption at 0.2.0 with missing mask layers, but the right thing to re-evaluate when EXELMJ's canvas starts dropping frames on large documents.

entries.name: Vello (GPU, linebender/vello)
entries.what_it_is: 'A GPU compute-centric 2D renderer', 4.3k stars. Requires a GPU with compute shader support, accessed through wgpu; targets 'all environments which can support WebGPU with the default limits'. Workspace contains vello, vello_encoding, vello_shaders, vello_tests, glifo, sparse_strips, xtask.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT (dual) — About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No prebuilt wasm. Rust + wasm-pack, AND it needs WebGPU at runtime. In Electron that means enabling the WebGPU flag and accepting driver-dependent behaviour on user machines. (c) Unmeasured.
entries.language_stack: Rust + WGSL compute shaders via wgpu.
entries.last_activity: Very active, 4.3k stars.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: Text rendering is present but glyph-level; no shaper bundled. Neutral for Arabic (shape upstream).
entries.steal_this_idea: Nothing you can ship yet — but note WHAT ITS ROADMAP CALLS UNFINISHED, because it is a precise list of what is genuinely hard in a modern 2D renderer: 'blur and filter effects', conflation artifacts, GPU memory allocation strategy, and glyph caching. If a 4.3k-star, well-funded project still lists blur/filters as in-progress, that is strong evidence you should BUY blur/shadow from ThorVG or CanvasKit rather than build it in designApp.ts.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Listed for completeness and to record a NEGATIVE: it is explicitly ALPHA, blur and filter effects are still being implemented, and its own README warns the web is not a primary target and WebGPU implementations are incomplete. For an offline desktop app that must render reliably on unknown hardware, that is disqualifying today. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: DOMINATED for EXELMJ right now — resvg renders correctly everywhere with zero GPU requirements. Use vello_hybrid instead if you want the Vello architecture, or wait.

entries.name: canvaskit-wasm (Skia's official WASM build)
entries.what_it_is: 'A WASM version of Skia's Canvas API' — the real Skia, the engine behind Chrome, Flutter and Android. Registry JSON verified: version 0.41.1 (dist-tags latest = 0.41.1, so the brief's 0.41.1 IS still the newest npm build), license BSD-3-Clause, main bin/canvaskit.js, dist.unpackedSize 25,542,718 bytes. Skia's own docs describe it as 'a core set of Skia canvas/paint/path/text APIs' drawing to a hardware-accelerated backend, plus Skottie (Skia's Lottie player).
entries.license: BSD-3-Clause — from the npm registry `license` field on 0.41.1. Fully permissive, satisfies your constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) PREBUILT ON NPM — no toolchain required for the stock builds. (c) EXACT SIZES, read off unpkg for 0.41.1/bin: canvaskit.wasm = 7.16 MB (core), canvaskit.js = 121 kB, plus bin/full/ = 8.2 MB and bin/profiling/ = 9.65 MB as separate flavours. THE BRIEF ASKS ABOUT VARIANTS BEYOND THE 0.41.1 NPM BUILD: yes, they exist, but only via self-compilation. Skia's modules/canvaskit README documents ./compile.sh with feature-strip flags — the README's own worked example is `./compile.sh no_skottie no_font`, and it states such a stripped build 'is about half the size of the default release build', i.e. roughly 3.5 MB. Other documented knobs cover fonts, Skottie/Lottie and the 'extras'. So a bespoke ~3-4 MB CanvasKit is achievable with an Emscripten + depot_tools build, which is a real but one-off cost. (h) Init is ASYNC — CanvasKitInit() returns a Promise.
entries.language_stack: C++ (Skia) via Emscripten; ships .d.ts type definitions on npm.
entries.last_activity: npm latest 0.41.1; Skia upstream is continuously developed but the npm publishing cadence has slowed markedly.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) POTENTIALLY THE ONLY WASM ENGINE HERE THAT SHAPES ARABIC ITSELF. Skia's paragraph module (SkParagraph) is built on HarfBuzz and ICU, which is precisely full shaping + bidi + line breaking. CAVEAT I MUST FLAG: I could not confirm from the CanvasKit README or skia.org page that the SHIPPED npm 0.41.1 build includes the paragraph/ICU components rather than only the simpler text APIs — the docs pages I fetched did not enumerate it, and my search budget ran out. Verify empirically before betting on it: load bin/canvaskit.js and check for CanvasKit.ParagraphBuilder and CanvasKit.TypefaceFontProvider. If present, you get shaped Arabic AND bidi with zero extra dependencies, which no other engine in this sweep offers in a prebuilt package. The ICU data is also the main reason the binary is 7 MB.
entries.steal_this_idea: SkImageFilter as a COMPOSABLE GRAPH rather than a fixed list of effects. Blur, drop shadow, colour matrix and blend are all nodes you chain, so 'drop shadow' is literally offset ∘ blur ∘ flood ∘ composite. If you implement effects in designApp.ts, implement them as a tiny composable node graph from day one — the same four primitives then give you glow, inner shadow, and every filter your users will ask for next, instead of three hardcoded functions.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) The most complete PATH API in this sweep — full Skia SkPath, SkPaint, SkCanvas semantics. (e) Stroke-to-path (SkPaint::getFillPath), dashes via SkPathEffect, all joins/caps, clipping, AND boolean path ops via SkPathOps built in. (f) THE MOST COMPLETE ANSWER TO EXELMJ'S BLUR/SHADOW/BLEND BLANK: SkImageFilter gives blur and drop shadow, SkBlendMode gives the complete CSS/SVG blend set, and colour-matrix/composite filters cover the rest. (g) possibly shaped Arabic, see notes. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: REPLACES IT OUTRIGHT ON CAPABILITY — everything resvg does plus an interactive path API plus effects plus booleans plus Lottie via Skottie. It loses ONLY on size: 7.16 MB vs 2.48 MB. For an OFFLINE DESKTOP Electron app where the wasm sits on local disk and never crosses a network, 7 MB is a nearly irrelevant cost — this is the key insight. Size objections that make sense for a web page do not apply to EXELMJ. This is my strongest 'one dependency solves everything' recommendation, with ThorVG as the lean alternative.

entries.name: pathkit-wasm (Skia PathOps, standalone)
entries.what_it_is: 'A WASM version of Skia's PathOps toolkit'. Registry JSON verified: version 1.0.0, license BSD-3-Clause, main bin/pathkit.js, dist.unpackedSize 379,752 bytes. This is Skia's battle-tested boolean path engine extracted as a standalone module: union / intersect / difference / xor / reverse-difference on arbitrary Bézier paths, plus path simplification, stroke-to-fill conversion and SVG path-string parsing/serialising.
entries.license: BSD-3-Clause — from the npm registry `license` field on 1.0.0.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) PREBUILT ON NPM, no toolchain. (c) EXACT SIZES from unpkg for 1.0.0/bin: pathkit.wasm = 324 kB, pathkit.js = 33.3 kB. That is 357 kB total for industrial-strength boolean ops. (h) Init is async (PathKitInit returns a Promise), but you call it ONCE at startup; every op after that is synchronous and instant, so it composes fine with a synchronous Canvas2D loop.
entries.language_stack: C++ (Skia PathOps) via Emscripten; plain JS API with a Path2D-like surface.
entries.last_activity: 1.0.0 — stable and essentially finished; PathOps in Skia itself is mature and continuously fuzzed.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: Not applicable — pure geometry, no text. Which means it is perfectly Arabic-safe: feed it outlines produced from shaped Arabic and it will union/subtract them correctly.
entries.steal_this_idea: Even if you take nothing else from this sweep, take this: robust boolean ops on Bézier paths are a genuinely hard numerical problem (self-intersections, coincident edges, fill-rule interactions, near-tangent curves) that has eaten years of engineering in every vector editor ever written. Skia's PathOps is the most fuzzed implementation in existence. DO NOT WRITE YOUR OWN. 324 kB is a rounding error against the months this saves.
entries.why_useful_for_us: THIS IS THE SINGLE HIGHEST VALUE-TO-SIZE ITEM IN THE WHOLE SWEEP. An 'Illustrator-like vector designer' is not credible without Pathfinder-style Unite/Minus Front/Intersect/Exclude, and NOTHING ELSE in this list provides them: ThorVG has no booleans, PlutoVG has none, tiny-skia lists 'Advanced Bézier path operations' as out of scope, kurbo has none, vello has none, resvg has none. pathkit-wasm provides exactly that gap, permissively licensed, prebuilt, offline, framework-free, in 324 kB. It ALSO does stroke-to-fill conversion, covering the 'Outline Stroke' command. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: PURELY COMPLEMENTARY, ZERO OVERLAP — resvg rasterises, PathKit does geometry. Adopt both. If I could only recommend one new dependency from this entire sweep, it would be this one.

entries.name: kurbo (linebender)
entries.what_it_is: Rust 2D curve library, 986 stars, version 0.13.1 released 13 Jul 2026. Verified from docs.rs that it exposes a `stroke` function AND `stroke_with`, plus the types Stroke, StrokeOpts, Join, Cap and a Dashes type alias — i.e. real STROKE EXPANSION (stroke-to-path outlining) with joins, caps and dashes. Also BezPath, an `offset` module for 'Computation of offset curves of cubic Béziers', analytic area via Green's theorem, bounding boxes and flattening. Emphasises 'accuracy and good performance in high-accuracy conditions'.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT — stated on docs.rs for 0.13.1 and in the About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate, no prebuilt wasm; wrap with wasm-bindgen. (c) Tiny — this is a geometry library with no rasteriser, so a wasm wrapper exposing stroke expansion would be measured in tens of kB. no_std capable (needs `std` or `libm`, and an allocator).
entries.last_activity: 0.13.1 on 13 Jul 2026; it is the shared geometry foundation for vello, vello_cpu and the wider linebender stack, and bezier-rs's maintainer now recommends migrating TO kurbo.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: Not applicable — pure geometry, hence Arabic-safe.
entries.steal_this_idea: Stroke expansion as a PURE FUNCTION path -> path, decoupled entirely from any rasteriser. Kurbo's stroke() takes a BezPath plus Stroke params and returns a new BezPath. That separation is why the same code can feed a CPU rasteriser, an SVG exporter, a PDF writer and a boolean-op engine. In designApp.ts today, stroking almost certainly happens inside your draw call; pulling it out into a pure geometry function is a small refactor that immediately makes 'Outline Stroke', accurate stroke bounding boxes, and correct stroked-shape booleans all possible.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (e) STROKE-TO-PATH OUTLINING WITH JOINS/CAPS/DASHES — one of only two verified sources in this sweep (with tiny-skia's PathStroker), and the higher-accuracy one. Also offset curves, which is the primitive behind Illustrator's Offset Path. (d) It is NOT a renderer — no fill/stroke/clip rasterisation, so it does not replace anything, it feeds things. (f) No blur, no filters, no blend. (h) Fully synchronous. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: ORTHOGONAL — resvg cannot do stroke expansion for you as a reusable operation at all. Worth wrapping if you go the Rust route; if you go the C++/prebuilt route, pathkit-wasm's stroke-to-fill covers the same need with no toolchain.

entries.name: raqote (jrmuizel/raqote)
entries.what_it_is: 'A pure Rust 2D Graphics Library' — small, simple, fast software 2D graphics, 1.2k stars. Verified feature list: path filling, stroking, dashing, image/solid/gradient fills, RECTANGULAR AND PATH CLIPPING, BLEND MODES, LAYERS, image repeat modes, and global alpha. API is DrawTarget + PathBuilder with move_to/line_to/quad_to/cubic_to/close, then fill/stroke. StrokeStyle carries caps, joins, width, miter limit, dash array and dash offset. Used as a rendering backend by resvg, Servo and orbtk.
entries.license: BSD-3-Clause — read from the About sidebar. (Note: this corrects the common assumption that it is MIT.) Permissive, satisfies your constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate, no prebuilt wasm and no npm package; build with wasm-bindgen. (c) Unmeasured, but it is a compact pure-Rust software rasteriser with no font stack or SVG parser, so expect a small wasm — comparable to or smaller than tiny-skia.
entries.last_activity: UNVERIFIED — the GitHub page fetch did not surface a last-commit date or a latest release, and my search budget was exhausted before I could confirm. Treat maintenance status as unknown; tiny-skia is the better-maintained sibling in the same niche.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) No text support surfaced in the README at all. Neutral/safe for Arabic — it makes no Latin assumptions because it does not do text. You would shape upstream and feed outlines.
entries.steal_this_idea: LAYERS as a first-class rasteriser concept (push a layer, draw into it, pop it with an opacity and a blend mode). Most software rasterisers make you manage offscreen buffers by hand; exposing push_layer/pop_layer is what makes group opacity and group blend modes — the thing your layers panel implies — correct rather than approximate. Note that group opacity is NOT the same as per-shape opacity, and users notice.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) Full PATH API. (e) Dashing, caps, joins, miter limit, plus BOTH rect and path clipping; no boolean ops and no stroke-to-path outlining. (f) HAS BLEND MODES AND LAYERS — partial credit against EXELMJ's blend blank — but NO blur, NO drop shadow, NO SVG filters. (h) Synchronous CPU rasterisation. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS in principle (it has the path API resvg lacks) but is LARGELY DOMINATED BY tiny-skia, which occupies the identical niche with the identical licence family, more blend modes (29, enumerated), a real PathStroker, active linebender maintenance, and the enormous advantage that it is already inside the wasm you ship. Include raqote in the sweep for completeness; pick tiny-skia in practice.

entries.name: femtovg
entries.what_it_is: 'GPU Antialiased 2D vector drawing library written in Rust', 931 stars — the Rust successor to NanoVG. Requires OpenGL ES 3.0+, with an additional WGPU backend. Supported: antialiasing, gradients, COMPOSITION MODES, global alpha, PATH HIT TESTING, colour fonts, text filling and stroking, TEXT SHAPING, text alignment. Explicitly NOT supported: 'Stroke dashing', 'Path scissoring', custom shaders, 3D transforms.
entries.license: MIT AND Apache-2.0 (dual) — from the About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate, no prebuilt wasm/npm. Browser use means wasm32 + WebGL2 (its GLES3-class backend), which the repo page did not explicitly confirm. (c) Unmeasured.
entries.last_activity: 931 stars; latest release not shown on the repo page I fetched.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) It advertises 'Text shaping' as a feature, which is more than most engines here claim — but the repo page did NOT name the shaping crate (rustybuzz/harfrust/swash) and did NOT document Arabic or bidi. UNVERIFIED AND HIGH RISK for an Arabic-first app: 'text shaping' in a graphics library frequently means kerning and ligature substitution for Latin, not Arabic joining plus bidi reordering. Do not adopt on the strength of that word alone — inspect its Cargo.toml for a shaper dependency first.
entries.steal_this_idea: 'Path hit testing' shipped as a core renderer feature. Same lesson as LunaSVG's elementFromPoint: in an editor, 'what did the user click' is a RENDERER question (it must respect fill rule, stroke width, transforms and clip) and gets subtly wrong answers when implemented separately in UI code. Route hit-testing through the same path/transform code as drawing.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) Path API in the NanoVG/HTML5-canvas idiom. (e) SIGNIFICANT GAP: stroke DASHING is explicitly unsupported, and so is path scissoring (clipping) — two things an Illustrator-like editor genuinely needs. No booleans, no stroke-to-path. (f) Composition modes yes; blur, drop shadow and SVG filters are NOT documented at all. (h) GPU/immediate mode; needs a GL context, so it does not slot into a Canvas2D pipeline without restructuring. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS on interactivity but is a POOR FIT overall — missing dashing and clipping are hard blockers for vector authoring, the GL requirement adds driver risk in Electron, and its shaping claim is unverified. Prefer ThorVG (which also has WebGL/WebGPU backends AND dashing AND clipping AND blur).

entries.name: NanoSVG (memononen/nanosvg)
entries.what_it_is: 'Simple stupid SVG parser', 2.0k stars. Two pieces: a PARSER that converts an SVG file into a flat list of CUBIC BÉZIER SHAPES (handling viewBox and px/pt/pc/mm/cm/in units), and a separate companion RASTERIZER that 'only renders flat filled shapes', intended for baking icons into textures. Single-header C: copy nanosvg.h, define NANOSVG_IMPLEMENTATION. Dependencies: stdio.h, string.h, math.h only. The repo header states 'This project is not actively maintained.'
entries.license: Zlib — from the About sidebar. Permissive, satisfies your constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No prebuilt wasm, but it is a SINGLE HEADER with three libc dependencies — this is the single easiest emcc target in this entire sweep, genuinely a one-command build producing a very small module. (c) Expect a wasm in the tens of kB, an order of magnitude below everything else here.
entries.last_activity: NOT ACTIVELY MAINTAINED per the repo's own header. That is acceptable for a frozen, feature-complete parser and unacceptable for a rasteriser you depend on.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) No text support whatsoever — SVG <text> is not handled. Arabic is simply out of scope. Never use it on documents containing live text; run those through resvg/usvg (which outlines text with shaping) first.
entries.steal_this_idea: THE OUTPUT FORMAT IS THE PRODUCT. NanoSVG's real contribution is normalising all of SVG's shape zoo — rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, arcs, elliptical arc flags — down to one uniform list of CUBIC BÉZIERS. Your design module already fits cubic Béziers in its image-tracing code, so this is the same representation you already own. Adopting 'everything becomes cubics at the door' as an invariant kills an entire class of bugs where one code path handles ellipses and another forgets to.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) NOT a general path API and NOT a full renderer — its rasteriser only does flat filled shapes (no gradients, no proper stroking). But as a PARSER it is excellent and tiny. (e)/(f) Nothing: no stroke-to-path, no booleans, no dash fidelity, no filters, no blur, no blend modes. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: DOMINATED AS A RENDERER, USEFUL AS A PARSER. resvg out-renders it in every dimension. Its narrow value for EXELMJ is as a dependency-free, tens-of-kB SVG-to-cubics front end for simple icon assets where spinning up a 2.48 MB wasm is disproportionate. Given you already ship resvg, that value is marginal — this entry mostly serves to close the category honestly.

entries.name: NanoVG (memononen/nanovg)
entries.what_it_is: 'Small antialiased vector graphics rendering library for OpenGL', 5.7k stars, 806 forks. The API deliberately follows the HTML5 canvas conventions: nvgBeginPath, nvgMoveTo, nvgBezierTo, nvgRect, nvgCircle, nvgFillColor, nvgFill, nvgStroke, nvgScissor, plus composite paths with even-odd fill and explicit path winding. Uses stb_truetype (optionally FreeType) for fonts via fontstash, and stb_image for images. Backends: OpenGL 2.0, OpenGL ES 2.0, OpenGL 3.2 core, OpenGL ES 3; requires a stencil buffer. The repo states 'This project is not actively maintained.'
entries.license: Zlib — from the About sidebar. Permissive, satisfies your constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No prebuilt wasm/npm. Emscripten + WebGL is feasible (its GLES2/GLES3 backends map onto WebGL1/WebGL2) but it is an unmaintained C project, so you own the port. (c) Unmeasured; the core is small (a few thousand lines) so the binary would be modest.
entries.last_activity: NOT ACTIVELY MAINTAINED per the repo's own statement. femtovg is the maintained Rust descendant.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) DISQUALIFYING FOR ARABIC AS-IS. Its text goes through fontstash + stb_truetype, which is a glyph atlas with simple codepoint-to-glyph mapping and NO shaping engine — the exact 'assumes pre-shaped Latin runs' failure mode the brief warns about. Arabic renders as isolated, unjoined letterforms in visual order. Fixable only by replacing the whole text layer with harfbuzz.
entries.steal_this_idea: nvgBoxGradient — NanoVG's trick of faking drop shadows and soft glows with a BOX GRADIENT (a rounded-rect gradient with a feather parameter) instead of a real Gaussian blur. It is not a correct blur, but it is nearly free, needs no offscreen buffer, and is visually convincing for the 90% case of UI drop shadows. For EXELMJ this is a genuinely valuable cheap path: your UI-builder's shadow previews can use a box-gradient approximation for interactive feedback and only invoke a real ThorVG/CanvasKit Gaussian blur on export. Also worth stealing: nvgScissor as a stack-based clip discipline.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) Clean HTML5-canvas-shaped PATH API — the most familiar API surface in this sweep for someone already writing Canvas2D. (e) Scissor clipping and winding/even-odd; dashing NOT documented, no booleans, no stroke-to-path. (f) No true blur, no SVG filters, no documented blend modes — only the box-gradient approximation described above. (h) Immediate-mode GPU, requires a GL context with stencil. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS in concept, DOMINATED in practice — unmaintained, needs a hand-rolled Emscripten port, has no shaping (fatal for Arabic-first), and lacks dashing and effects. Included as the ancestor of femtovg and for the box-gradient idea, which is the genuinely transferable part.

entries.name: harfbuzzjs
entries.what_it_is: 'Minimal version of HarfBuzz for JavaScript use' — the actual HarfBuzz text shaping engine compiled to WebAssembly, published by the HarfBuzz project itself. Registry JSON verified: name harfbuzzjs, version 1.6.0, license MIT, main dist/index.mjs, dist.unpackedSize 1,224,078 bytes, repository github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzzjs.
entries.license: MIT — from the npm registry `license` field on 1.6.0. (HarfBuzz proper is 'Old MIT'.) Satisfies your constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) PREBUILT .WASM ON NPM — npm i harfbuzzjs, no toolchain. (c) 1.22 MB unpacked for the package; the hb.wasm itself is a fraction of that. (h) Module instantiation is async, then all shaping calls are SYNCHRONOUS — which is exactly what a synchronous Canvas2D design module needs: await once at boot, then shape inline during layout.
entries.language_stack: C++ (HarfBuzz) via Emscripten, ESM entry point.
entries.last_activity: 1.6.0, published by the upstream harfbuzz org.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) THIS IS THE ANSWER TO THE ARABIC PROBLEM. Every C/C++/Rust rasteriser in this sweep except CanvasKit and resvg either has no text at all (tiny-skia, raqote, vello_cpu, NanoSVG) or has glyph-level text with no shaper (ThorVG, PlutoVG, Blend2D, NanoVG). harfbuzzjs is the missing piece: it does GSUB/GPOS-driven Arabic joining (init/medi/fina/isol), ligatures, mark positioning for diacritics, and returns glyph ids with x/y advances and offsets. It is THE reference implementation — the one all the Rust ports are ports OF. Note it does SHAPING, not BIDI: you still need the bidi/paragraph-direction layer, which designApp.ts already has in its Arabic bidi runs.
entries.steal_this_idea: Decouple SHAPING from RASTERISATION completely, and make the interface between them 'glyph id + position'. Once you accept that boundary, the engine choice stops being an Arabic question — ThorVG, PlutoVG, tiny-skia, vello_cpu and pathkit all become viable because none of them ever sees a string. That single architectural decision converts the brief's hardest constraint ('an Arabic-first app cannot use an engine that assumes pre-shaped Latin runs') from a disqualifier into a non-issue, because YOU become the thing that pre-shapes.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Not a rasteriser, but the entry that makes the rest of the sweep usable. Without it, the (g) column disqualifies most of this list; with it, (g) becomes irrelevant to engine selection. Combine as: harfbuzzjs (shape) -> glyph outlines -> ThorVG/PlutoVG/pathkit (draw, effect, boolean). VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS — resvg shapes Arabic only inside its own one-shot SVG pipeline and will not shape text for YOUR canvas. harfbuzzjs will.

entries.name: HarfRust (harfbuzz/harfrust)
entries.what_it_is: 'A Rust port of HarfBuzz text shaping engine', matching HarfBuzz v14.3.0, maintained under the official harfbuzz GitHub org. Started as a fork of RustyBuzz to move from ttf-parser onto read-fonts (the Fontations ecosystem), with subsetting provided by skera. Passes the HarfBuzz test and fuzzing suites.
entries.license: MIT — from the About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate; no prebuilt wasm. In practice you get it for free by building resvg/usvg to wasm, since usvg 0.48.1 lists harfrust as its shaping dependency. (c) Small relative to a rasteriser.
entries.last_activity: Active — it is the officially designated successor to rustybuzz, which was archived on 26 Jul 2026 with a note recommending HarfRust.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) Shapes Arabic via the standard OpenType path (GSUB/GPOS). Its documented conformance gap is 'No Arabic fallback shaper', which requires building lookups on the fly — READ THIS PRECISELY: it means Arabic in fonts that LACK OpenType Arabic features will not be synthesised. Any real Arabic font (Noto Naskh/Kufi, Amiri, Cairo, Dubai, IBM Plex Sans Arabic, Tajawal…) ships init/medi/fina/isol in GSUB and shapes correctly. So this is a non-issue provided EXELMJ bundles its Arabic fonts, which an offline app must do anyway.
entries.steal_this_idea: The migration signal itself: rustybuzz ARCHIVED on 26 Jul 2026 pointing at HarfRust, and usvg 0.48.1 already depends on harfrust. If EXELMJ pins any Rust text stack, pin harfrust, not rustybuzz — and note that your currently shipped @resvg/resvg-wasm 2.6.2 is on the OLD rustybuzz lineage. That is a concrete, dated reason to rebuild resvg from current source.
entries.why_useful_for_us: The Rust-side answer to (g) if you go the wasm-pack route instead of the Emscripten route. Also the reason a self-built current resvg is better than the npm 2.6.2 build for Arabic. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: it is a COMPONENT OF the newer resvg, so 'complements' — but the finding that matters is that your shipped resvg build predates it.

entries.name: rustybuzz (ARCHIVED — what your current build actually contains)
entries.what_it_is: Rust port of HarfBuzz shaping, matching harfbuzz v10.1.0, passing 2221 of 2252 harfbuzz shaping tests. Runs 1.5-2x slower than C harfbuzz. Documented gaps: no Arabic FALLBACK shaper, subsetting removed, no `mort` table, no avar2/boring-expansion-spec, no external font-loading integration, and malformed fonts error rather than falling back.
entries.license: MIT — from the About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: Rust crate. You are already shipping it transitively inside @resvg/resvg-wasm 2.6.2's index_bg.wasm.
entries.last_activity: ARCHIVED 26 JULY 2026. The maintainers explicitly recommend switching to HarfRust. This is a hard end-of-life, three weeks before today's date.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) Shapes Arabic correctly for fonts with proper OpenType Arabic GSUB features — 2221/2252 harfbuzz conformance is high. The 'No Arabic fallback shaper' line has been widely misread as 'no Arabic support'; it is not. It means no synthesis for fonts missing the features. Bundle real Arabic fonts and it is fine.
entries.steal_this_idea: Nothing technical — but a maintenance lesson worth acting on: a dependency you never touch can be archived under you. Your Arabic rendering correctness currently rests on an archived crate buried inside a wasm blob you did not build. Put a note in PROJECT_MAP.md's [ORPHANS & PENDING] section and schedule the resvg rebuild.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Included because it is a FACT ABOUT YOUR EXISTING STACK, not a proposal: @resvg/resvg-wasm 2.6.2 (MPL-2.0) rasterises through tiny-skia and shapes through rustybuzz, and rustybuzz was archived on 26 Jul 2026. Combined with the upstream relicense to Apache-2.0 OR MIT, that gives two independent reasons to rebuild resvg from linebender/resvg source rather than staying on the npm package. VERDICT: this is the incumbent's hidden expiry date.

entries.name: cosmic-text (pop-os)
entries.what_it_is: 'Pure Rust multi-line text handling' — shaping, layout and rendering wrapped in one abstraction, 2.1k stars. Verified: it uses HarfRust for shaping and a custom implementation for layout that handles BIDIRECTIONAL TEXT, with Arabic explicitly demonstrated in the project's own screenshots. Rendering goes through swash (ligatures, colour emoji). Its focus is shaping + layout, not rasterisation.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT (dual) — from the About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate; no prebuilt wasm. wasm-bindgen wrap required. WASM compatibility is not documented on the repo page (unverified), though as pure Rust it should compile — the practical risk is font enumeration (fontdb wanting system font directories), which you sidestep in an offline app by embedding font bytes. (c) Unmeasured.
entries.language_stack: Rust; harfrust + swash + a custom bidi-aware layout engine.
entries.last_activity: 2.1k stars, actively developed as part of the COSMIC desktop; already migrated to HarfRust, which indicates current maintenance.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) STRONGEST STANDALONE ARABIC STORY IN THE SWEEP AFTER resvg/usvg — it does BOTH shaping (harfrust) AND bidi (custom layout), plus multi-line wrapping, which is the part everyone forgets: Arabic line breaking with mixed LTR runs is where naive implementations fall apart. Since designApp.ts already has 'text boxes with Arabic bidi runs', this is the closest off-the-shelf match to a component you have already hand-written, and worth reading even if you never link it.
entries.steal_this_idea: Buffer/Attrs/Shaping as a layered API: attributes (family, weight, style, colour) are ranges over the text, shaping runs are computed per bidi+script+font segment, and LAYOUT LINES are produced separately from GLYPH RUNS. That three-level split — attributed text -> shaped runs -> laid-out lines -> positioned glyphs — is the model that makes mixed Arabic/English text boxes with per-run styling actually work. Compare it against your current bidi-run implementation; the place hand-rolled implementations usually break is that they fuse the bidi split and the font-fallback split into one pass, when they must be separate passes.
entries.why_useful_for_us: If you ever replace designApp.ts's hand-written Arabic text box layout, this is the reference implementation to move to or to copy from. It is a text engine, not a rasteriser: it emits positioned glyphs, which any engine in this list can then draw as outlines. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS — resvg only shapes text that is inside an SVG document it is rendering; cosmic-text shapes and lays out YOUR interactive, editable text boxes, which is a different and, for a designer app, more important job.

entries.name: swash (dfrg/swash)
entries.what_it_is: Rust font introspection, complex shaping and glyph scaling library, 865 stars. Verified from the README: it implements the UNIVERSAL SHAPING ENGINE for complex scripts (Devanagari, Malayalam, etc.) and explicitly lists 'Arabic joining including Urdu style climbing runs'. Its scaling side provides 'Scalable outlines with full variation support (TrueType and Postscript)', 'Path effects (stroking and dashing)' and transforms including synthetic emboldening.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT (dual) — from the About sidebar.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate; no prebuilt wasm. Reachable transitively through cosmic-text. (c) Unmeasured. wasm/no_std support is not documented on the repo page (unverified).
entries.language_stack: Rust; its own shaper, NOT a harfbuzz port.
entries.last_activity: 865 stars; used by cosmic-text for rendering. Latest release not shown on the page I fetched.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) NOTABLE: it is an INDEPENDENT shaper, not a harfbuzz port, and it names Arabic joining explicitly — including Urdu climbing runs, which is a genuinely advanced case (nastaliq-style descending letter sequences) that most shapers get wrong. That specific claim is a strong signal the Arabic implementation is serious rather than nominal. Verify against your actual bundled fonts before committing.
entries.steal_this_idea: The fact that ONE crate does shaping AND outline extraction AND stroking/dashing of those outlines. That combination is the whole 'convert text to outlines, then treat it as a shape' pipeline in a single dependency. It also confirms the correct pipeline shape for EXELMJ: shape -> outline -> (optionally stroke-expand) -> hand to rasteriser or boolean engine. Note it does path effects on GLYPH outlines specifically, which is how you get correctly-stroked Arabic display type.
entries.why_useful_for_us: The alternative to harfrust if you want shaping AND glyph-outline extraction from one crate rather than assembling a stack. For EXELMJ's 'convert Arabic text to outlines for SVG/PDF export' need, swash covers shaping and outlines in a single dependency. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: COMPLEMENTS — it serves your interactive text, not resvg's document rendering. Lower confidence than harfrust/harfbuzzjs only because I could not verify wasm support or release cadence.

entries.name: lyon (nical/lyon)
entries.what_it_is: Rust path TESSELLATION library — 'turn complex paths into triangles for use in your own rendering engine', 2.6k stars, 1,640 commits. Fill tessellation confirmed via FillTessellator in its own example; SVG-compliant path handling; custom vertex formats. The README is emphatic that 'Lyon is not an SVG renderer' and that it lacks built-in antialiasing.
entries.license: Apache-2.0, MIT AND MPL-2.0 — the About sidebar lists all three. All are on your permitted list.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) Rust crate, no prebuilt wasm. It produces vertex/index buffers, so in a browser you would feed them to WebGL/WebGPU yourself. (c) Small — it emits geometry, it does not rasterise.
entries.framework_lock: None — but it implies you own the GPU rendering layer.
entries.last_activity: 2.6k stars, 1,640 commits; latest release not shown on the page I fetched.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: Not applicable — pure geometry, hence Arabic-safe. Feed it outlines from a shaper and it will tessellate Arabic glyphs like any other path.
entries.steal_this_idea: The clean separation between TESSELLATION and RENDERING, and specifically that antialiasing is deliberately NOT the tessellator's job. If EXELMJ ever goes GPU, this is the boundary to draw: geometry generation is deterministic, cacheable and testable; antialiasing is a rendering-technique choice (MSAA, analytic coverage, supersampling) that should be swappable without regenerating geometry. Also worth stealing: its stroke tessellator treats a stroke as a geometry-generation problem, which is the same 'stroke is geometry, not a draw flag' insight as kurbo's.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) NOT a rasteriser and NOT a path-drawing API — it is the geometry stage of a GPU renderer you would write yourself. Stroke tessellation, dashes and joins/caps were NOT confirmed on the repo page (its crates/ layout implies a StrokeTessellator exists, but I did not verify). No booleans. (f) Nothing — no blur, filters or blend; those are your shader's problem. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: NOT COMPARABLE, and DOMINATED as a solution for EXELMJ, because adopting it means writing your own GPU renderer — precisely the work ThorVG, CanvasKit and vello_hybrid already did. Listed to close the category and because its licence trio is unusually accommodating.

entries.name: Rive Runtime (rive-app/rive-runtime)
entries.what_it_is: Rive's open-source runtime, which INCLUDES the 'Rive Renderer' — described as 'a state-of-the-art vector renderer for Metal, Vulkan, D3D12, D3D11, and OpenGL/WebGL'. It is a modern GPU vector rasteriser using pixel-local-storage techniques. Builds to WebAssembly via `build_rive.sh ninja release wasm`. The runtime also exposes an abstract Renderer interface so an external renderer can be hooked in.
entries.license: MIT — reported in the About sidebar, and the fetch found NO separate, more restrictive licence carve-out for the renderer component (this was worth checking specifically, because the Rive Renderer was historically under different terms before being opened up).
entries.embeddable_how: (b) No npm package for the raw renderer; you compile with the provided wasm build target (ninja + Emscripten). (c) Unmeasured. Practical blocker below.
entries.language_stack: C++ with Metal/Vulkan/D3D/GL/WebGL backends; ninja build.
entries.framework_lock: None at the C++ level; the JS ecosystem around it is Rive-format-centric.
entries.last_activity: Active commercial-backed development.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) Rive's text features go through its own text engine tied to the Rive format. Not a general shaping service you can drive, and not verified for Arabic. Treat as unsuitable for EXELMJ text.
entries.steal_this_idea: The abstract `Renderer` interface: Rive's file/animation layer is fully decoupled from rasterisation, so the same document plays back on Metal, Vulkan, D3D or WebGL by swapping one implementation. If EXELMJ defines its own narrow Renderer interface (moveTo/cubicTo/fill/stroke/clip/pushLayer/popLayer/blur), it can start on Canvas2D, add a ThorVG wasm backend, and later a GPU backend, WITHOUT touching designApp.ts's 2,900 lines. Given this sweep offers several plausible engines and no clear permanent winner, that interface is the correct insurance policy — and it is the single most actionable recommendation here after pathkit-wasm.
entries.why_useful_for_us: (d) THE BLOCKER: it does NOT expose a generic vector path API. It is tightly coupled to Rive's .riv format, artboards and animation system — you drive it with Rive files, not with moveTo/cubicTo. That makes it unusable as EXELMJ's drawing engine despite a genuinely excellent renderer and an MIT licence. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: NOT A REPLACEMENT AND NOT A COMPLEMENT for the rasteriser role. Its transferable value is architectural (the Renderer interface) plus, if you ever want a second animation format alongside Lottie, .riv playback.

entries.name: Adobe SVG Native Viewer (adobe/svg-native-viewer)
entries.what_it_is: Adobe's open-sourced SVG parser/renderer for user-interface graphics, 164 stars, 40 forks, 129 commits. Implements 'SVG Native', a strict subset of SVG 1.1/2.0 that deliberately EXCLUDES scripting, interactions, events, animations, filters, masks, patterns and TEXT. Ships six renderer ports behind one parser: StringSVGRenderer (testing), CGSVGRenderer (CoreGraphics), SkiaSVGRenderer, CairoSVGRenderer, GDIPlusSVGRenderer and D2DSVGRenderer. C++11 (C++14 for the Skia port); requires CMake and Boost.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 — confirmed ('licensed under Apache V2'). Satisfies your constraint.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) NO wasm build mentioned anywhere. Requires Boost, which is a heavyweight and awkward Emscripten dependency. Effectively native-only without real porting work. (c) Unmeasured.
entries.last_activity: 129 commits, 164 stars — genuinely obscure, but also low-velocity.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) TEXT IS EXCLUDED FROM THE FORMAT ENTIRELY. Not an Arabic risk so much as an Arabic impossibility — you would outline all text before it ever reaches this renderer.
entries.steal_this_idea: THE PORT-PER-BACKEND ARCHITECTURE, which is the best-documented instance of the Renderer-interface idea in this sweep: ONE parser, SIX rasterisers (CoreGraphics, Skia, Cairo, GDI+, Direct2D, plus a string renderer that just SERIALISES THE DRAW CALLS). That last one is the gem — StringSVGRenderer turns rendering into a text dump, which makes the renderer GOLDEN-FILE TESTABLE without any pixel comparison. For EXELMJ, implementing a 'string renderer' behind your drawing interface gives you fast, deterministic, cross-platform regression tests for the design module (which currently has 92 tests) without rasterising anything or fighting antialiasing differences between machines.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Honest verdict: NOT ADOPTABLE. No wasm, Boost dependency, and the SVG Native subset excludes exactly the features an Illustrator-like editor needs (filters, masks, patterns, text). Included because it satisfies 'obscure but permissive', because the brief implies wanting the category closed, and above all because its testing architecture is worth copying. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: DOMINATED IN EVERY DIMENSION — resvg supports a far larger SVG subset, has filters, has shaped text, and ships a prebuilt wasm.

entries.name: cairo + pixman (REFERENCE / INSPIRATION ONLY — licence fails your constraint)
entries.what_it_is: The classic C 2D vector graphics library and its low-level pixel-compositing companion. Backends verified from cairographics.org: Xlib, XCB, Quartz, Win32, image buffers, PostScript, PDF and SVG output. Cairo's model (path construction, save/restore, source/mask/destination compositing, Porter-Duff operators) is the direct ancestor of PlutoVG's API — you can see the lineage clearly in plutovg.h.
entries.license: EXPLICITLY FLAGGED AS A CONSTRAINT FAILURE. cairographics.org states cairo is released under the user's choice of 'GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL) version 2.1' OR 'Mozilla Public License (MPL) version 1.1'. Your permitted list is MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD / MPL-2.0 / ISC — LGPL-2.1 is not on it, and MPL-1.1 is NOT MPL-2.0 (different licence, not on your list either). THEREFORE: REFERENCE AND INSPIRATION ONLY. Do not link cairo into EXELMJ. Pixman is separately licensed and is commonly MIT — rlottie's COPYING file corroborates a distinct 'PIX (Pixman License)' for its vendored copy — but I could NOT fetch pixman's own COPYING to confirm the SPDX, so treat pixman's licence as UNVERIFIED and do not rely on it either.
entries.embeddable_how: Native C library. Emscripten ports of cairo exist in the wild but are unofficial. Irrelevant given the licence position — do not embed.
entries.language_stack: C, with pixman for software compositing.
entries.last_activity: Mature/slow; largely in maintenance as GTK and others move on.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) Cairo's 'toy' text API does no shaping at all; real Arabic in the cairo world comes from pango + harfbuzz sitting on top. That layering is itself the lesson: even the canonical C 2D library concluded that shaping does NOT belong in the rasteriser.
entries.steal_this_idea: The SOURCE / MASK / DESTINATION model. Cairo formalised the idea that every drawing operation is: take a SOURCE pattern (colour, gradient, image), filter it through a MASK (the shape's coverage, or an alpha mask, or a clip), and composite onto the DESTINATION with an operator. Under that model, fill, stroke, clip, group-opacity and text all reduce to one operation with different masks. Nothing else here explains so cleanly WHY plutovg's operator enum, tiny-skia's Mask, ThorVG's MaskMethod and raqote's layers all look the way they do. If you are designing EXELMJ's internal drawing interface, design it as source/mask/destination and every engine in this list becomes a straightforward backend.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Zero direct use — LABELLED REFERENCE ONLY per your rules, because the licence fails. Its value is that it is the conceptual source code of the entire category: PlutoVG is a modern MIT reimplementation of essentially cairo's ideas, so if you adopt PlutoVG you can read cairo's (excellent, decades-refined) documentation to understand what you are holding. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: not applicable — cannot be adopted.

entries.name: @napi-rs/canvas (native Skia in the Electron MAIN process — the non-wasm escape hatch)
entries.what_it_is: 'Canvas for Node.js with skia backend'. Registry JSON verified: version 1.0.6, license MIT, main index.js, dist.unpackedSize 125,557 bytes, repo github.com/Brooooooklyn/canvas, with prebuilt platform binaries as optionalDependencies for darwin-x64/arm64, linux x64/arm64 gnu+musl, arm-gnueabihf, riscv64, WIN32-X64-MSVC AND WIN32-ARM64-MSVC, and android-arm64. Sibling option: skia-canvas 3.0.8, MIT, 'A multi-threaded, GPU-accelerated, Canvas API for Node', unpackedSize 179,051, github.com/samizdatco/skia-canvas.
entries.license: MIT — from the npm registry `license` field on 1.0.6. skia-canvas 3.0.8 is likewise MIT.
entries.embeddable_how: (b) NOT WASM — this is a NATIVE N-API addon, which is why the tiny 125 kB package pulls a platform binary. That is a feature, not a bug, for Electron: it runs in the MAIN process at full native speed with no wasm size or startup cost, and prebuilt Windows x64 and arm64 binaries mean no compilation on your target platform. (h) Synchronous Canvas2D-compatible API, no init await — the closest drop-in to your existing Canvas2D code in this entire sweep.
entries.language_stack: Rust + Skia via napi-rs; exposes the standard Canvas 2D API surface.
entries.last_activity: 1.0.6, actively maintained with broad platform coverage.
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: (g) Being real Skia, it inherits Skia's text stack. Whether the bundled build includes full harfbuzz+ICU paragraph shaping is UNVERIFIED — @napi-rs/canvas exposes the Canvas2D fillText API, which in browsers implies shaping, but the addon's exact Skia configuration was not confirmed. Test with an Arabic string before relying on it. If it falls short, outline Arabic upstream with harfbuzzjs as with everything else.
entries.steal_this_idea: That an Electron app has TWO runtimes, and heavyweight rendering does not have to live in the renderer. Route interactive drawing through Canvas2D/wasm for latency, and route EXPORT (PDF/PNG/SVG at print resolution, batch operations, the Illustrator COM round-trip) through a native Skia process over IPC. Export is where you want blur, blend modes, correct colour and speed, and where a 200 ms async round-trip is invisible to the user. This resolves the entire wasm-size-versus-capability tension without compromising either side.
entries.why_useful_for_us: The pragmatic alternative to every wasm option here: full native Skia (path API, PathOps booleans, SkImageFilter blur and drop shadow, all blend modes, stroke-to-path) with ZERO wasm binary in your bundle and a synchronous Canvas2D-shaped API. Costs: native binaries per platform (prebuilt, including Windows x64/arm64 — you are on Windows 11), and it lives in the main process so the renderer talks to it over IPC. (f) FULLY CLOSES the blur/shadow/blend blank for the export path. VERDICT vs @resvg/resvg-wasm: REPLACES IT FOR EXPORT/RASTERISATION and dominates it on capability, while resvg keeps its niche as the in-renderer, dependency-free SVG importer. Strongly worth prototyping alongside ThorVG before committing to either.

domain: Support layers for deliverable (b), the Illustrator-like vector designer: (1) colour science, (2) document model + undo history, (3) spatial index for hit-testing/marquee, (4) vector FILE IMPORT. VERDICTS ON THE DECIDING QUESTIONS — [OKLCH/OKLab/P3 gradient interpolation] culori (interpolate + fixupHueShorter + samples, all 30 modes incl. oklch/oklab/p3/rec2020) and colorjs.io (Color.range with premultiplied alpha + hue methods) both do it natively; @texel/color does NOT ship an interpolate() but ships test/example-interpolation.js (verified HTTP 200) which lerps in OKLCH, gamut-maps with gamutMapOKLCH, serializes, and paints into a Canvas2D created with {colorSpace:'display-p3'} — that ~40-line file is the whole recipe and is the single most copyable artefact in this sweep. [CSS Color Level 4 ROUND-TRIP] only colorjs.io and culori do a real round-trip (parse any CSS4 string -> serialize back, incl. color(display-p3 ...) and oklch()); chroma-js is partial; @texel/color's deserialize() is documented as "intentionally limited" (hex, rgb(), rgba(), oklch(), oklab(), plain color() with no modifiers) so it is a converter, not a parser — pair it with culori for I/O. [CMYK / ICC — the hard ceiling] VERIFIED BY SOURCE: colorjs.io has NO cmyk space (src/spaces/cmyk.js -> 404) and culori has NO cmyk mode (src/cmyk/definition.js -> 404, absent from src/bootstrap/all.js). chroma-js has src/io/cmyk but it is naive device-CMYK arithmetic, not colour-managed. So a *real* print path needs a CMS, and two permissive ones exist: lcms-wasm (MIT, Little-CMS submodule also MIT, 579 KB total, ships a CMYK->sRGB demo) and — the better find — jscolorengine (MPL-2.0, v1.4.4 published 2026-05-02, 100% JS with optional WASM-SIMD, ICC v2+v4, RGB/CMYK/Lab/XYZ/3CLR/4CLR, all four rendering intents, black-point compensation, soft-proof, and portable baked-LUT JSON via Transform.fromJSON). MPL-2.0 is on your allow-list, so the CMYK ceiling is liftable. [DOC MODEL] loro-crdt is the standout and needs zero networking: its .d.ts confirms LoroTree/LoroTreeNode with moveBefore/moveAfter/index() (a real movable-tree CRDT = your layer tree), LoroMovableList, LoroDoc.checkout(frontiers)/checkoutToLatest/fork/forkAt (time travel + branches), and an UndoManager with setMergeInterval (coalesces a drag into one step), addExcludeOriginPrefix (keep selection changes out of the undo stack), and onPush/onPop metadata (store the selection with the step) — but it costs a ~3.18 MB wasm. If you will not pay that, mutative gives you strictly RFC-6902-compliant patches + inversePatches with zero deps and no wasm. [SPATIAL] rbush for the live scene (dynamic insert/remove), flatbush for the frozen/imported layer (static, one ArrayBuffer, transferable to a Worker). [IMPORT] pdf.js src/display/svg.js is GONE (404 on master) — the SVG backend was removed, so PDF/.ai vector import must go through page.getOperatorList() + the OPS enum, which still carries constructPath:91, moveTo:13, curveTo:15, rectangle:19, fill:22, setFillRGBColor:59. .ai specifically is covered by @opendesign/illustrator-parser-pdfcpu (Apache-2.0). No permissive JS EPS/PostScript parser was found at all — Ghostscript/pstoedit are (A)GPL, REFERENCE ONLY. .fig has a brand-new MIT option (openfig-core, published 2026-08-01) which supersedes the widely-cited fig-kiwi — and fig-kiwi has NO LICENCE FIELD AT ALL, so it is legally unusable, reference only.

entries.name: culori
entries.what_it_is: Comprehensive colour library with 30 registered modes (oklab, oklch, okhsl, okhsv, p3, rec2020, prophoto, a98, lab65, lch65, luv, lchuv, jab, jch, itp, xyb, dlab, dlch, cubehelix, hsi, yiq, lrgb, xyz50, xyz65, ...) plus interpolation, colour difference, blending and CSS Color Level 4 parse/serialize. Verified: src/p3/definition.js, src/oklch/definition.js and src/interpolate/interpolate.js all return 200; src/cmyk/definition.js returns 404 and cmyk is absent from src/bootstrap/all.js — there is NO CMYK.
entries.license: MIT
entries.embeddable_how: npm package, zero runtime dependencies. Import the tree-shakeable procedural entry `culori/fn` (declared in package.json exports) rather than the default barrel; package.json sideEffects is an allowlist of exactly 3 files (src/index.js, src/bootstrap/all.js, src/bootstrap/css.js) so bundlers can drop every unused mode. 1.11 MB / 168 files unpacked, but that is the whole source tree — a realistic vite build pulling oklch+p3+rgb+interpolate is a few KB.
entries.why_useful_for_us: This is the default pick for the gradient/colour-picker layer. It is the only zero-dependency library here that does BOTH a real CSS Color 4 round-trip (parse arbitrary CSS strings, formatCss back out) AND perceptual gradient interpolation with proper hue fixup, which is exactly the pair of jobs a vector designer's gradient editor needs. Works fully offline, no account, framework-free.
entries.language_stack: Pure JavaScript (ESM source, CJS bundle), no wasm, no native
entries.last_activity: v4.0.2 published 2025-06-27; npm metadata modified 2026-04-03
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: N/A — no text handling
entries.steal_this_idea: The `useMode(definition)` registry pattern: colour spaces are inert data objects that must be explicitly registered, which is what makes the library genuinely tree-shakeable instead of just claiming to be. Copy this for EXELMJ's own effects/filters registry so unused shape types drop out of the renderer bundle.

entries.name: colorjs.io
entries.what_it_is: Lea Verou / Chris Lilley's reference-grade colour library — the de-facto executable spec for CSS Color Level 4/5. Verified space list from src/spaces/index-fn.js includes XYZ_D65, XYZ_D50, XYZ_ABS_D65, Lab, Lab_D65, LCH, sRGB, sRGB_Linear, HSL, HSL_P3, HSL_REC2020, HWB, HSV, P3, P3_Linear, A98RGB, ProPhoto, REC_2020, REC_2020_Scene_Referred, OKLab, OKLCH, OKLCH_P3, OKLCH_sRGB, OKLCH_REC_2020, OKLrab, OKLrCH, Okhsl, Okhsv, CAM16_JMh, HCT, Luv, LCHuv, HSLuv, HPLuv, Helmlab, HelmGen, HelmGenLCh, plus an HDR index. src/interpolation.js confirmed present; src/spaces/cmyk.js confirmed ABSENT (404).
entries.license: MIT
entries.embeddable_how: npm package, zero runtime dependencies. Two entry points declared in exports: the default object-oriented `colorjs.io` and the tree-shakeable procedural `colorjs.io/fn`, plus `colorjs.io/spaces`. 15.78 MB / 382 files unpacked — that number is docs + types + dist + src, not what ships; use the /fn entry and import only the spaces you touch.
entries.why_useful_for_us: The correctness oracle. When our own OKLCH gamut mapping or a gradient ramp looks wrong, this is what you diff against. Its Color.range()/mix() supports premultiplied alpha and explicit hue-interpolation methods (shorter/longer/increasing/decreasing) — the exact knobs Illustrator-style gradient stops need. Ship-wise it is heavier than @texel/color, so a sane split is: colorjs.io behind a dev/debug flag or on the Node/MCP side, @texel/color or culori in the renderer hot path.
entries.language_stack: Pure JavaScript ESM (+ CJS build), TypeScript declarations shipped, no wasm
entries.last_activity: v0.7.1 published 2026-07-24 — very active
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: N/A
entries.steal_this_idea: Its ColorSpace class models each space as {id, name, base, coords, fromBase, toBase, formats} — a declarative graph where conversion is a path-find over `base` links rather than an N^2 matrix of hand-written converters. If EXELMJ ever adds a second document colour space, copy this graph-of-spaces design instead of writing pairwise converters.

entries.name: @texel/color
entries.what_it_is: Matt DesLauriers' minimal modern colour library. README claims (and ships a bench script for) 'approx 5-125 times faster than Colorjs.io', zero allocations in conversion/gamut-mapping hot paths (all functions take an `out` array), and ~3.5 KB minified if you only pull OKLCH->sRGB. Spaces: xyz, xyz-d50, oklab, oklch, okhsv, okhsl, srgb, srgb-linear, display-p3(+linear), rec2020(+linear), a98-rgb(+linear), prophoto-rgb(+linear). Has gamutMapOKLCH implementing Björn Ottosson's 2021 gamut clipping with five strategies (MapToL, MapToGray, MapToCuspL, MapToAdaptiveGray, MapToAdaptiveCuspL) and findCuspOKLCH for per-hue precomputation.
entries.license: MIT
entries.embeddable_how: npm package, ZERO dependencies, pure ESM source shipped uncompiled (main: ./src/index.js). 111 KB / 21 files unpacked — the smallest serious option here. Tree-shakes per-space automatically because every space is a separate named export.
entries.why_useful_for_us: This is the one to put in the renderer's hot path — colour-picker drag, live gradient ramp repaint, per-frame swatch preview — precisely because it allocates nothing. Confirmed limitation you must plan around: deserialize() is documented as 'intentionally limited ... complex CSS color string handling is not within the scope of this library' (hex, rgb(), rgba(), oklch(), oklab(), plain color() with no modifiers only), and there is NO CMYK. Pair it with culori or colorjs.io for file I/O and CSS round-tripping.
entries.language_stack: Pure JavaScript ESM, JSDoc-generated .d.ts, no wasm, no build step
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: N/A
entries.steal_this_idea: test/example-interpolation.js (verified to exist, HTTP 200): convert both endpoint colours into a shared OKLCH interpolation space with reusable scratch arrays tmpA/tmpB, lerp L and C but lerpAngle the hue, gamut-map the result with gamutMapOKLCH against DisplayP3Gamut or sRGBGamut depending on what the display supports, serialize(), and fill into a Canvas2D obtained via getContext('2d', {colorSpace: 'display-p3'}). That is a complete wide-gamut gradient-ramp renderer in ~40 lines with zero per-pixel allocation — copy it verbatim into the gradient tool even if we never install the package. Also steal findCuspOKLCH: precompute the cusp once per hue, then gamut-map thousands of stops on that hue for free.

entries.name: chroma-js
entries.what_it_is: Gregor Aisch's long-running colour conversion + scale library. Verified present in source: src/io/cmyk/index.js, src/io/oklch/index.js, src/io/css/index.js. Strong at scales/bezier/correctLightness and ColorBrewer palettes.
entries.license: (BSD-3-Clause AND Apache-2.0) — that exact compound string is the package.json license field; the repo LICENSE is a BSD-3-Clause with a name-endorsement clause (Gregor Aisch), the Apache-2.0 half covers the bundled ColorBrewer/palette data. Both halves are permissive and on our allow-list.
entries.embeddable_how: npm package, zero dependencies, 397 KB / 121 files. ESM + CJS. Modular builds exist but tree-shaking is weaker than culori/@texel — the API is a chainable wrapper object.
entries.why_useful_for_us: Useful mainly for its scale/palette machinery (chroma.scale().mode('oklch').correctLightness()) if we ever build automatic swatch-ramp generation from a single brand colour. Its CMYK support is REAL CODE but NAIVE device-CMYK arithmetic with no ICC profile involved — do not let anyone mistake it for a print path. If you need print-accurate CMYK use jscolorengine or lcms-wasm instead.
entries.last_activity: v3.2.0 published 2025-11-28
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: N/A
entries.steal_this_idea: correctLightness(): after building a multi-stop scale, iteratively re-space the stops so perceived L* advances linearly across t. This is what stops auto-generated swatch ramps from having a dead flat zone in the middle, and it is ~20 lines.

entries.name: @radix-ui/colors
entries.what_it_is: A static, hand-tuned colour SCALE system: ~30 hues x 12 steps, each with a light scale, a dark scale, and alpha variants, shipped as plain CSS custom-property files plus JS objects. Not a colour-maths library — there are no conversion or interpolation functions at all.
entries.license: MIT
entries.embeddable_how: npm package, zero dependencies, sideEffects:false, 620 KB / 137 files. Files are per-scale CSS (amber.css, amber-dark.css, amber-alpha.css, amber-dark-alpha.css, blue.css, bronze.css ...) plus JS objects — import only the scales you use, or just copy the CSS files into src/design/ and never install the package.
entries.why_useful_for_us: This is the swatches/tokens answer, not the colour-science answer. It gives the vector designer's default palette and the UI chrome's semantic steps (step 9 = solid brand, step 11 = text) for free, with light/dark pairs already solved. IMPORTANT VERIFIED CAVEAT: I extracted the v3.0.0 tarball and grepped it — there are ZERO P3 files in it. Any claim that Radix ships display-p3 variants does not hold for the published v3.0.0 package. If we want P3 swatches we must generate them ourselves (with culori or @texel/color).
entries.language_stack: CSS custom properties + plain JS objects
entries.framework_lock: None despite the @radix-ui scope — the colors package is pure data and has no React dependency
entries.last_activity: v3.0.0 published 2023-10-02 (npm metadata modified 2025-12-24) — effectively frozen but complete; vendorable as flat CSS
entries.rtl_arabic_notes: N/A — colour data only, direction-agnostic
entries.steal_this_idea: The 12-step semantic contract: steps 1-2 backgrounds, 3-5 component backgrounds (normal/hover/active), 6-8 borders, 9-10 solid fills, 11-12 text. Adopting this numbering for EXELMJ's own tokens means every future component knows which step to reach for without a designer in the loop, and light/dark swap becomes a single variable-block change.

entries.name: jscolorengine (jsColorEngine)
entries.what_it_is: A full ICC colour-management engine written in 100% JavaScript with optional WebAssembly SIMD kernels for the bulk image path. Supports RGB, CMYK, Lab, XYZ and 3CLR/4CLR device spaces; ICC v2 AND v4 profile loading (both LUT-based and matrix-shaper); built-in virtual profiles (sRGB, AdobeRGB, Lab, XYZ); all four rendering intents; black-point compensation; trilinear and tetrahedral interpolation; multi-step transforms; custom pipeline stages spliced in at the PCS; deltaE76/deltaE2000; and a LUT-free f64 mode for prepress work where deltaE matters more than throughput. Claims (with a runnable benchmark) to beat native C LittleCMS on 3 of 4 image workflows.
entries.license: MPL-2.0 (repo LICENSE is the Mozilla Public License 2.0 text; package.json license field reads "mpl-2.0") — explicitly on our allow-list. File-level copyleft only: we may link it into EXELMJ and keep our own files proprietary, we just must publish modifications to ITS files.
entries.embeddable_how: npm package `jscolorengine` (v1.4.4), zero runtime dependencies. package.json declares a `browser` field that stubs out child_process/fs/path/util, so it bundles cleanly for a renderer; also ships a prebuilt browser bundle (browser/jsColorEngineWeb.js). Explicitly claims Node, browsers, Electron, web workers, React Native. No native bindings, no compile step.
entries.why_useful_for_us: THIS IS THE ANSWER TO THE CMYK CEILING. Nothing else in the entire 8-sweep corpus gives an Illustrator-like designer a genuine print path. With this we can: load a real CMYK output profile (ISO Coated / SWOP / Japan Color), soft-proof the canvas on screen, show an out-of-gamut warning per swatch, and export CMYK values that a printer will actually honour. Being pure JS with an optional-not-required wasm kernel, it degrades gracefully and stays 100% offline.
